item.title: CoFI workshop at ASEG Discover 2024
item.description:
Preparations are well underway for InLab’s workshop at ASEG Discover 2024. Attendees will be provided with a hands-on experience of InLab’s emerging geoscience inference softwared ecosystem centred around CoFI, InLab’s common framework for inference. The following link allows to register for ASEG Discover 2024 and our workshop asegdiscover.com.au/registration

More information about the workshop is available here

InLab’s commitment to FAIR software means that all the workshop material will be made available here.

item.title: EGU 2024 CoFI Poster
item.description: InLab researchers have recently presented several new research results at the European Geosciences Union meeting in Vienna, 15 Apr. There were talks on BayesBay, our new Trans-dimensional inference platform available through CoFI, and also a progress report on development of an ‘Independent state’ sampler, which will become part of CoFI in the future. We also presented an updated CoFI poster (see below) and discussed with European researchers how they might become engaged with the CoFI community.

item.title: Sub22 CoFI Workshop
item.description:
InLab held its first hands-on public workshop centred around CoFI at the National Wine Centre in Adelaide with attendees from industry, government and academia. The workshop complemented sub22, the CSIRO’s Deep Earth Imaging Future Science Platform organised biennial subsurface imaging conference.

Attendees gained hands-on experience with CoFI and have since started to solve their inference problem using InLab’s emerging geoscience inference ecosystem by forking Espresso and installing CoFI. If you missed the workshop fear not, InLab’s commitment to open source means that all the workshop material is available here.

item.title: IAMG 2022 CoFI Poster
item.description:
Poster presentation details

Date: 29 Aug - 3 Sept, 2022

Venue: Nancy, France

Title: CoFI - Linking geoscience inference problems with tools for their solution

Description:

Inference problems in the geosciences vary significantly in size and scope, from 1D regression of geochemical data, to building 3D models of Earth’s interior structure. As such, the combination of datasets and the approaches used for solving are often highly problem-specific. Some researchers develop inversion and parameter estimation algorithms that suit their needs and wonder where else they could be applied. Others focus on developing new and flexible forward models of Earth phenomena and want a complementary inversion algorithm that fits their needs. Many more of us have data and questions to answer and need both.

item.title: CoFI
item.description:
The development of CoFI is now being supported through an AuScope 2021 Pilot Project.

In the Common Framework For Inference project (CoFI), researchers will build an open and flexible software platform that enables the wider research community to more effectively undertake inversion (a tool to understand subsurface properties using field data). CoFI will also help educators to better teach inversion to geophysics students through the provision of interactive examples.

CoFI will be the world’s first independent transportable framework for inversion, offering researchers a flexible high-level programming language that expresses inversion problems and connects them to solutions. Project leader, Professor Malcolm Sambridge from The ANU explains why this is so exciting:

item.title: 2020 Gutenberg Lecture
item.description:
The American Geophysical Union has awarded the 2020 Gutenberg Lecture to Prof. Malcolm Sambridge.

The Beno Gutenberg Lecture is presented annually in recognition of outstanding contributions to the field of seismology. The lecture is named to honor the life and work of renowned seismologist Beno Gutenberg and is presented during the AGU Fall Meeting.
